Technically yes, but the rules file calls this identifier permanent, so it would be a deliberate exception to that rule, and it only makes sense if nobody outside your own machines has installed the app yet.

**What breaks if installed copies exist**
- **Accessibility permission:** macOS ties the grant to the bundle ID, so every existing user would see the app as new and have to re-grant it. For a dictation app that is the core feature, so it looks like a broken update.
- **Sparkle updates:** the update path from `is.waiwai.dictation` to the new ID is risky. Sparkle expects the update's bundle ID to match the installed app, so existing installs may not auto-update across the rename. I'd test this before relying on it. The EdDSA key itself is unaffected, so keep it as is.
- **Local data:** UserDefaults/preferences, Keychain items, Application Support folders, login-item registration and any caches are keyed to the old ID and would appear reset unless you write a migration.

**What stays the same**
- The Sparkle EdDSA key stays, and the inside-out signing rule still applies. You'd just re-sign and re-notarize under the new ID.

**Recommendation**
- **No users yet** (only you and a few testers): rename now. It's the cheapest it will ever be, and testers can re-grant permission once. Before the rename, update the "Release invariants" section in the rules file, plus `docs/release.md` and `AGENTS.md`, so they don't tell future sessions to refuse it.
- **Real users on the old ID:** keep `is.waiwai.dictation`. The branding gain isn't worth the permission reset. The ID is invisible to users, so the product name can still be OpenRamble.

Which is it? If nobody outside your team has the app, I can list every place the old ID appears (project settings, entitlements, appcast, Info.plist, scripts, docs) and make the rename a single change once you confirm.
